turns.prompt_text: I would like to make some chicken tikka masala I have paprika Menudo spice mix And Tulsi I'm here at Hy-Vee in Ames. What else do I need?
turns.response_html:
To make a classic Chicken Tikka Masala, you will need to pick up a few core components for the marinade and the creamy tomato sauce.

Since you have paprika (great for the signature color and mild sweetness) and Tulsi (holy basil, which has a nice peppery, clove-like flavor you can use as a unique garnish), you have a head start. The Menudo spice mix usually contains chili, garlic, onion, and oregano—it will add savory heat, though the oregano might give it a slightly different twist than traditional Indian flavors.

To get that authentic flavor, here is what you should grab while walking through Hy-Vee:

Produce Aisle:

  • Yellow onion (1 large)
  • Fresh garlic (1 head)
  • Fresh ginger (a small knob)
  • Fresh cilantro (optional, if you prefer the traditional garnish over the Tulsi)

Meat Department:

  • Boneless, skinless chicken (about 1.5 to 2 lbs; thighs are recommended as they stay juicier, but breasts work perfectly fine too)

Dairy Aisle:

  • Plain yogurt (full-fat is best for the chicken marinade; avoid Greek if possible as it can be too thick, or thin it out slightly)
  • Heavy whipping cream (for the rich sauce)
  • Unsalted butter or Ghee

Pantry & Canned Goods:

  • Canned crushed tomatoes or tomato sauce (one 15 oz can or a larger 28 oz can depending on how saucy you like it)
  • Tomato paste (just a small can or tube for depth of flavor)
  • Cooking oil (canola, vegetable, or olive oil)

Spice Aisle:

  • Garam Masala (This is the most crucial spice blend for the authentic Tikka Masala flavor, as it has cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and cumin).
  • Ground turmeric
  • Ground coriander (optional, but highly recommended)
  • Ground cumin (optional, but highly recommended)
  • (Don't forget to make sure you have salt at home!)

To Serve (Optional but recommended):

  • Basmati rice
  • Naan bread (usually found in the bakery or the international foods aisle)
